triage.note: D12 (postmortem 2026-08-25 §8, interviewer-feedback gap 3): item offsets index `normalized_text`, not the raw filing, and until this case nothing said so to a consumer and nothing let one check it. ADR-026 §a refuses a raw-to-normalized offset map, so the remedy is a CONTRACT — serve the exact text the offsets index, publish a sha that binds the download to the run, and carry the slicing recipe verbatim where a consumer will read it. The check pins all three: LIVE, that `build_view`'s `norm_sha256` is the sha256 of the run's own UTF-8 `normalized_text` and that `normalized_text[start:end]` is byte-for-byte the `text` the API serves for that item, on every spanned item of an HTML-era and a txt-era fixture; LIVE, that the same offsets against the RAW bytes produce something DIFFERENT on every one of those items, so the documented warning is falsifiable rather than decorative; and by allow-list pin, that `/api/normalized/{token}` exists exactly once and that every expression on the path from this run's `normalized_text` to the response body is present WHOLE — what goes into the cache, which slot comes back out, the response, the sha header — plus a guard that neither `_run` nor `api_normalized` rebinds `norm` after its pinned binding. The endpoint itself is unreachable from the harness (importing app.py drags fastapi into the dependency-free unit job, the same constraint check_boilerplate_plumbing works around), so what these pins establish is that the code says the right thing, NOT that FastAPI serves it; that half is unpinned and carries its own debt row. PR #54 R1 is why the wording is this careful: the first version pinned only the two expressions that MENTION `norm` and not where `norm` comes from, so `norm = hit[1]` — the endpoint serving the raw filing under a matching sha header — was green, which is the exact defect the check's own comment called impossible. Three mutations were watched red under the repaired pins on 2026-08-26 and green on revert: `norm = hit[1]`, `norm = (result.get("normalized_text") or "")[:100]`, and `norm = hit[2]` followed by a second `norm = hit[1]`. Watched red before implementation on 2026-08-26 with 17 failures: no `/api/normalized` route at all, all four wire pins at 0, all five recipe lines missing from each of README.md and app.py, and `norm_sha256=None` on both fixtures. Two halves were already GREEN in that red run and are here for the future, not for this change: the raw-differs half, which is a property of normalization (it goes red the day normalization becomes the identity, and then the docs get to stop shouting), and the slice-equals-served-text half, which is INV-S2 restated at the API boundary (it goes red the day the view serves a second copy instead of a slice — the drift the contract exists to prevent). What this change made true is the SERVED half: before it, there was no endpoint to perform step 2 against and no sha to perform step 3 with, so the recipe was unwritable, not merely unwritten.

provenance: Created 2026-08-26 for D12. Fixtures are the same HTML-era/txt-era pair `ui-boilerplate-exclusion` uses (msft-2013, ge-1994), chosen so the recipe is pinned across both normalizer paths rather than only the modern one; no fixture was added. The recipe text itself lives in `src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py::RECIPE` and the check requires it to appear exactly once in each of README.md and src/sec10k/web/app.py — app.py's copy is the `/api/normalized/{token}` docstring, which FastAPI serves as that endpoint's OpenAPI description, so the reader with no access to this repo gets the recipe at /docs. Comparison is whitespace-free (`_squash`), because the two copies wrap differently and how a sentence is wrapped carries no information. PR #54 R2 added a sixth doc pin, README-only: the worked snippet's step-4 line, which first shipped as a bare `==` that is false for any item longer than DISPLAY_MAX — aapl-2025 item 1A is 68,162 chars against a 40,000-char display copy, so the published recipe raised AssertionError one line below the fixture it printed. The line is pinned in its prefix form AND executed here against a genuinely truncated item; the case refuses to pass at all if no fixture in it has one, since on a corpus of short items the two forms agree and the pin would be vacuous. ge-1994 contributes 1 truncated item and msft-2013 contributes 2.
